bluf: QUIETER SUNDAY, ELEVATED NIGHTLIFE AND CYBER AWARENESS — Saturday's Texas-Florida game (Florida won 27-24; 103,989 in attendance) and Austin FC's 2-1 loss to Vancouver are over, and open-source reporting through 5 AM shows no significant downtown disturbance tied to either. Today is calm and sunny: high about 75F, light winds, no advisories. Event load is moderate: Livestrong Run for the Roses at Auditorium Shores (8 AM, road closures near Riverside), Texas Street Food Tour at Republic Square (1-9 PM), and Weezer at Moody Center (7 PM). Physical risk stays AMBER: the Oct 16 shooting inside a moving vehicle at W 10th and N Lamar remains under investigation (a possible suspect was questioned; no charges released), the Oct 13 bomb-note bank robbery at 111 Congress Ave is closed by arrest, and the Mar 1 Sixth Street attack (3 dead including the gunman, 14 hospitalized, FBI treated as potential terrorism, reportedly linked to US action against Iran) is the standing precedent for bar-close risk. Cyber moves to AMBER: Microsoft reports hotel Wi-Fi captive-portal credential theft (resumed Sep 29) and Cofense reports fake guest-complaint emails to hotel front desks delivering remote-access malware. Civil unrest is low: Saturday's Austin No Kings event was a peaceful Halloween election fair; early voting begins Monday Oct 19. US-Iran: no settlement, indirect talks continue.

incidents.title: DOWNTOWN VIOLENCE / ROBBERY PATTERN - ONGOING
incidents.location: W 10th & N Lamar (~0.9 mi NW); 111 Congress Ave (~0.2 mi); E 6th & Sabine
incidents.relevance: The Congress Ave bank is roughly 0.2 mi from the property; the suspect is in custody, so no ongoing threat, but expect continued APD presence. The Oct 16 shooting appears targeted (occupants knew each other) and not a random-public threat. The recurring pattern is armed robbery and shootings in the bar-close window (about 1:30-3:00 AM, Saturday-Sunday), so brief concierge and valet to steer late walkers to rideshare.
incidents.detail: (1) Oct 16, ~7:18 PM: a driver was shot by someone inside his moving vehicle and crashed near W 10th St and N Lamar Blvd; he was taken into surgery. APD said everyone in the vehicle knew each other and a possible suspect was in custody and being questioned. No charges or identities had been released as of this brief. (2) Oct 13, 4:44 PM: Wells Fargo at 111 Congress Ave was robbed after a note claimed a bomb; an officer arrested Makiya Johnson, 26, 1 minute 54 seconds after the call, less than two blocks away. He faces two counts of robbery by threat and had a warrant for an Oct 10 aggravated robbery in a neighboring jurisdiction. No device was reported. (3) Sep 13, bar close at E 6th and Sabine: three off-duty soldiers were robbed at gunpoint (one shot, survived); three suspects were arrested Sep 22.

incidents.title: SIXTH STREET ATTACK PRECEDENT / US-IRAN WAR CONTEXT
incidents.location: W 6th & Rio Grande (~0.7 mi NW); national / Gulf region
incidents.relevance: No credible, specific threat to Austin or the property is identified today. The Mar 1 attack is the reason bar-close hours and entertainment-district crowds stay on the AMBER watch list: a lone actor tied to events abroad struck a crowded Saturday-night location. Escalation or a breakdown in talks is the trigger to reassess posture.
incidents.detail: On Mar 1, a gunman fired from an SUV and then on foot outside Buford's at W 6th and Rio Grande at about 1:59 AM, a day after the US-Israeli offensive on Iran began. Three people died (including the gunman, killed by APD within about a minute) and 14 were hospitalized; the FBI treated it as potential terrorism. The gunman wore Iranian-flag attire, and the Statesman reports he was motivated by US military action in Iran. The war is now about seven months old. The June memorandum collapsed; Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US lifts its blockade and eases pressure; President Trump rejected the plan but left room for talks. Qatar and Pakistan are mediating. Reporting is contradictory: Defense Secretary Hegseth warned Iran of 'destruction' while Iran's foreign minister demands 'credible guarantees' before talks resume.

incidents.title: HOSPITALITY CYBER CAMPAIGNS TARGETING HOTEL STAFF
incidents.location: Front desk, reservations, guest-relations inboxes; guest Wi-Fi
incidents.relevance: No compromise of the property is known. Front desk, reservations and concierge are the intended targets. Staff should not open complaint-email attachments or 'photo' links, and should report any captive-portal prompt asking for a software update or a device code. Ask IT to confirm MFA and conditional access on staff accounts.
incidents.detail: Two active campaigns: (1) Cofense (Oct 7) reports fake guest complaints and negative-review emails with links to a 'photo or video' that is really a Windows shortcut disguised as a JPG; it installs Node.js and the EtherRAT or TONResolver remote-access malware. (2) Microsoft says Storm-2945, a Midnight Blizzard (Russia SVR-linked) sub-cluster, resumed its CaptiveCrunch campaign Sep 29, tampering with hotel Wi-Fi captive portals to push fake updates and device-code login prompts that steal Microsoft 365 sessions; reporting ties the activity to managed service providers serving seven of the ten largest US hotel chains.

incidents.title: CAPITOL THREAT ARREST (SEP 30) - NO ONGOING THREAT
incidents.relevance: Informational: lone-actor threat pattern near downtown government sites. No change in posture.
incidents.detail: Texas DPS arrested Benny Caldera Jr., 40, of Converse on Sep 30 after credible information about a planned violent attack on the Capitol; he faces state terroristic-threat and federal charges. DPS said there is no ongoing threat to the Capitol, legislators, staff or the public.

civil_unrest.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Austin Events
civil_unrest.detail: Saturday's Austin event ('Don't Ghost the Vote' at First UU Church, 4700 Grover Ave) was a Halloween-themed election fair with sample ballots and polling information, not a march, per CBS Austin. A small rally also gathered outside a busy park in southwest Austin. Nationwide events run Saturday and Sunday and are nonpartisan; organizers prohibit weapons and civil disobedience. Early voting in Texas begins Monday Oct 19 and runs through Oct 30; Election Day is Nov 3. A 'Parade to the Polls' is planned for the coming week.

civil_unrest.title: Anti-ICE / Capitol-Area Activity
civil_unrest.detail: Tension persists after the Sep 20 shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez by an ICE officer: he was charged federally with assaulting and resisting a federal officer, and Rep. Casar and other members of Congress held a hearing on ICE's actions Oct 15. Capitol-area crowds have been small and peaceful (about 150-200). An anti-death-penalty rally was also held at the Capitol. No specific downtown action is announced for today; flash demonstrations remain possible (Capitol grounds close 8 PM).

notes: NWS Area Forecast Discussion (128 AM CDT Sun Oct 18): another crisp, cool fall morning; lows upper 40s to near 50 along and south of I-35 (low 40s in the Hill Country); highs in the 70s area-wide.
Unlike the past several days, winds are very light to almost calm under plentiful sunshine. Saturday's gusty northerlies (gusts to 35 mph) are gone; outdoor setups are no longer wind-limited.
Tonight: much warmer lows in the low to mid 50s with increasing clouds as southerly return flow arrives. No rain expected anywhere in the extended forecast.
Monday: upper 70s to low 80s. Tuesday onward: above-normal warmth, low 80s climbing to upper 80s/low 90s by the end of the week; dewpoints return to the 50s-60s (more humid).
Sunrise 7:35 AM, sunset 6:56 PM. UV index moderate (about 5) at midday; sun exposure advisory for the Auditorium Shores run and Republic Square festival crowds.
Regional: no flood or severe-weather concerns for Central Texas this week.

EXPECT a checkout surge from visiting Texas-Florida fans and weekend leisure guests: bell and valet at full strength 7-11 AM; confirm luggage hold and rideshare staging.

BRIEF front desk, reservations and concierge on the guest-complaint phishing campaign: do not open attachments or 'photo/video' links in complaint or review emails; forward to IT and Security. Report any guest Wi-Fi portal prompt for a software update or device code.
ASK IT to confirm MFA and conditional access on staff Microsoft 365 accounts and to check the guest Wi-Fi captive portal and managed-service-provider alerts.

MONITOR the Texas Capitol for flash demonstrations and Waterloo Park/Moody Center crowds; escalate to the duty supervisor if crowds exceed 200 or move toward downtown.

national_context: US-Iran war (about seven months): no settlement in force. Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table and demands credible guarantees against future attack; the US rejected the plan but signaled further talks; Qatar and Pakistan are mediating. Statements are contradictory (Hegseth threatens 'destruction'; Iran's president calls talks 'meaningless'). Austin has a direct precedent: the Mar 1 Sixth Street attack, which the FBI treated as potential terrorism.

Political climate: nationwide No Kings: Vote Early events (Oct 17-18) focus on turnout; Saturday's Austin event was peaceful. Early voting begins Oct 19; Election Day is Nov 3. Anti-ICE tension in Austin persists after the Sep 20 Garces Perez shooting.

Cyber: hospitality is a high-volume ransomware and phishing target (Qilin, Akira, Play, LockBit lead sector claims), with Midnight Blizzard hotel Wi-Fi and fake guest-complaint campaigns active this month.
